thread:
rachael: heads up, automatic publish failed on npm for js-sdk. semver-check blocked the tag because changelog includes 'BREAKING' word. did anyone add a breaking change?
ci-bot: [CI] release/js-sdk job failed: semver-check failed (exit 1). logs: https://ci.redwood.local/builds/1958001234
leo: I didn't. I only regenerated types for a doc example tweak. regen-diff link: https://artifacts.redwood.local/regen-diff-1958001234.txt
jen: quick look: the generated changelog entry says "Removes deprecated `fooBar` example — BREAKING". The script that converts openapi markers to changelog apparently tags removals as breaking by default.
rachael: that's aggressive. It was only an example in a sample app spec, not an actual model field removal.
regen-bot: [regen] auto-changelog created entry: "feat: update example; BREAKING: removed fooBar example" (file: changelogs/js-sdk.md)
leo: semver-check is doing the right thing if changelog contains BREAKING. But the upstream generator should avoid false positives.
jen: root cause: our openapi->changelog mapper treats any deletion in examples or vendor extensions as a breaking note. We should scope that to schema-level removals only.
release-guy: immediate options: 1) patch semver-check to ignore changelog tokens unless they originate from commit messages (preferable), 2) edit the changelog in the PR to remove 'BREAKING', 3) revert the regen commit and re-run.
rachael: editing changelog by hand is quickest to unstick the pipeline. but we need a long-term fix. we shouldn't have releases blocked by example changes.
leo: agree. I'll open a small PR to sanitize auto-changelog rules. regex fix: only mark as BREAKING when commit contains "BREAKING CHANGE:" or openapi change touches /components/schemas/.
jen: for the immediate release can someone push a branch that strips the word and re-triggers semver-check? I'll volunteer to pair on the PR edit.
ci-bot: [Comment] You can rerun semver-check via circleci: https://ci.redwood.local/retry/1958001234
release-guy: note: auto-publish will resume if semver-check passes. leaving pipeline paused until we patch generator.
rachael: I'll do the manual changelog edit and create a hotfix PR titled "chore(release): remove spurious BREAKING tag from js-sdk changelog". Assigning @jen to review.
leo: I'll make the generator patch PR: "fix(changelog): only treat schema removals as breaking (ignore example deletions)" and add tests. linking to ticket DEVEX-1157.
jen: after the hotfix merges, we still need to audit recent regen runs for other SDKs (python, go). I'll run `scripts/check-changelogs --scan` to list occurrences.
regen-bot: [scan] found BREAKING mentions in changelogs: js-sdk.md, py-sdk.md (one), go-sdk.md (none). Report: https://artifacts.redwood.local/changelog-scan-1958001234.json
rachael: good catch. jen, can you scrub py-sdk changelog too?
jen: on it. will push small edit and request quick approvals from owners.
release-guy: policy change captured: semver-check will be updated to prefer explicit commit-level BREAKING tokens; changelog parser will be fixed in next minor release. I'll open a follow-up RFC to change our release automation to require explicit BREAKING in commit body for major/minor bumps.
leo: timeline: hotfix edits in the next 30m, generator patch in the next day, CI policy RFC in a week.
rachael: thanks everyone. keeping the auto-publish paused until we've greened all sdks. ping here when done. :pray:
